summary: Kennard Lipman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979) and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Ballhatchet (1922–1995) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Clifton College and Peterhouse, Cambridge, later serving as Lecturer in the History of Modern India at SOAS (1948–1988) and Reader in Indian History at Oxford (1963–1965).
Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held an attested post at Stetson University in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. from the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later teaching at Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, under Aloysius Pieris, and earned a PhD at CUNY Graduate Center. He has held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Emmanuel College and under W. D. C. Wagiswara, later serving at Trinity College, YMCA College, Pacific School of Religion, and the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a philosophy professor at the University at Buffalo and chaired the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. S. Ch'en (1907–1993) studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, Yenching, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, he held posts at Harvard, UCLA, and as Professor of Buddhism at Princeton (1961–1971).

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stanford, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Tokyo, and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held professorships at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University.

Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held an academic post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Somerled Macdonald (1832–1903) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He was educated at the University of Aberdeen and New College, Edinburgh, and later held posts at the University of Calcutta and the United Free Church Mission.

Kenneth W. Jones (1934–1996) was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Stockton University and UC Berkeley under Thomas Metcalf and Wolfram Eberhard, later serving on the faculty at Kansas State University from 1965, becoming Distinguished Professor in 1989.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned literature doctorates at the University of Tokyo. He has served on the faculties of Aichi Gakuin University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history. He earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University and is an emeritus professor at Hanazono University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Bukkyo University. He served as professor at Koyasan University, Seizan College, and Shuchiin University, and was named emeritus professor at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a professor (attested in 2006).

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He held an attested post as associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (2015–2016).

Kenyu Mitomo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees at Rissho University and studied at UC Berkeley. Between 1968 and 2015, he served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.
Kerry Martin Skora is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held attested posts at the University of Virginia in 1996 and Southern Methodist University in 1998.
